candidate.title: No vector for a verifier that writes a complete, schema-valid `allow` and is then killed by an unsolicited signal
candidate.claim: §7.2 lists 'death by signal / crash' as an unconditional deny and §7.2 precedence text requires `signal_death` to be classified distinctly from `nonzero_exit`, but the only signal vector in set 0.6.0 (`host-deny-killed-by-signal`) kills the verifier BEFORE any output. The exit-code sibling (`host-deny-nonzero-exit-after-allow`) exists, the signal sibling does not. That is exactly the ordering a lazy host gets wrong: it parses stdout first, sees a perfect `{"verdict":"allow"}\n`, then checks the exit status with a comparison that treats a signal death as success. In Node the `close` event delivers `code === null` when the child died by signal, so `if (code > 0) deny()` is skipped; in Python `returncode` is negative (`-11` for SIGSEGV), so the same `> 0` guard also passes. Both are fail-open on a verdict the spec says MUST be denied. The attack is a verifier whose native proof library segfaults or is OOM-killed in teardown after the verdict flush (§5.1 explicitly anticipates native libraries misbehaving on fd 1; nothing says they finish exiting cleanly), or a presenter who can influence verifier teardown timing. Observable a vector can assert: verifier writes `{"verdict":"allow"}\n`, flushes, then raises SIGSEGV on itself; host MUST deny and, if it reports a class, MUST report `signal_death`, not `allow` and not `nonzero_exit`.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: 'The host MUST treat all of the following as deny, regardless of what (if anything) reached stdout: ... death by signal / crash;'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: 'death by an unsolicited signal and a non-zero exit are distinct conditions (`signal_death` vs `nonzero_exit`, §16.3) — a host MUST NOT collapse them into one classification.'

Conformance vector index (set 0.6.0): 'host-deny-killed-by-signal: ... the verifier terminates via an unsolicited fatal signal before produ[cing output]' and 'host-deny-nonzero-exit-after-allow: the verifier prints a syntactically valid `allow` and then ex[its non-zero]' — no vector combines a complete allow with a subsequent signal death.

Node.js child_process docs, 'close' event: 'code <number> The exit code if the child exited on its own... null if the process was killed by a signal' — https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#event-close
Python subprocess docs: 'A negative value -N indicates that the child was terminated by signal N (POSIX only)' — https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.Popen.returncode

Reproduce the fail-open host pattern in an isolated scratch dir: `node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process');const c=spawn('sh',['-c','printf \\'{\"verdict\":\"allow\"}\\n\\'; kill -SEGV $$']);let o='';c.stdout.on('data',d=>o+=d);c.on('close',(code,sig)=>{console.log('code',code,'signal',sig,'naive-verdict',(code>0)?'deny':JSON.parse(o).verdict)})"` — prints `code null signal SIGSEGV naive-verdict allow`.
candidate.proposed_artifact: A new host_behavior conformance vector `host-deny-signal-death-after-allow` (verifier stub emits a complete newline-terminated `allow`, flushes, then self-delivers SIGSEGV; expected decision deny, expected failure class `signal_death`) staged as a fixture diff pinned to a4f546f, plus the matching one-line addition to the §16.3 offered-case list.

score.reason: Pinned §7.2 unconditionally rejects signal death, while the existing signal fixture emits no verdict, confirming a bounded additive vector that catches stdout-first fail-open handling.

candidate.title: Architecture pseudocode is not marked informative and contradicts the §7.2 failure-classification precedence and the closed verdict schema
candidate.claim: Refinement of the iteration-1 candidate that was dropped on artifact shape, not merit. The draft's Section 3 pseudocode is introduced only as 'Language-neutral pseudocode for the host side' with no RFC-style '(non-normative)' marker, so a reader may treat it as the implementation of the MUSTs. It diverges from the normative text in three checkable ways: (1) it tests `status != 0` before `timed_out(child)`, whereas the contract's §7.2 precedence for reported classification is output-bound kill, then timeout, then signal death, then non-zero exit, then parse/schema — and §7.2 says a host MUST NOT collapse signal death and non-zero exit, yet the pseudocode has no signal-death branch at all; (2) `for entry in (verdict.consume_nonces or [])` silently accepts an empty `consume_nonces` array that the closed §3.4 schema (`minItems: 1`) requires the host to reject (vector host-deny-empty-consume-nonces); (3) no schema-validation step appears between parse and the switch, so an unrecognized `kind`, an extra property, or an out-of-registry `code` would be relayed — the exact relay behavior §denial-codes now forbids. The fix is textual: label the block '(informative)', add a `validate_schema(verdict) or reject("schema_invalid")` step, add a `signaled(child)` branch, and reorder branches to match §7.2 or add a sentence that ordering in the sketch is illustrative and §7.2 governs.
evidence: draft-kondoju-evc-01 §Architecture: "Language-neutral pseudocode for the host side:" followed by `if status != 0: reject("non-zero exit")` then `if timed_out(child): reject("timeout")` then `verdict = parse_single_json_object(out)` then `for entry in (verdict.consume_nonces or []):` — no signal-death branch, no schema check.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: "classify the cause it acted on in this precedence: its own kills first (output bound, then timeout), then an unsolicited signal death, then a non-zero exit, and only then the stdout parse and schema checks ... a host **MUST NOT** collapse them into one classification."
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 allow schema: `"consume_nonces": {"type":"array","minItems":1, ...}` with `"additionalProperties": false`

candidate.title: Request-write failure (EPIPE) when the verifier exits before consuming stdin is not a listed §7.2 condition; hosts crash, deny, or relay
candidate.claim: §2 obligates the host to write the whole request then close stdin, and §6 obligates the verifier to stop reading at its bound and emit `malformed_input` — which means a conforming verifier will routinely exit while the host is still writing a large request, closing the pipe under the host's write. §7.2's enumerated fail-closed conditions cover exit status, timeout, signal death, and stdout shape, but not failure of the host's own request delivery. Three reasonable hosts diverge: (1) a Node host with no `error` listener on `child.stdin` gets an unhandled EPIPE and crashes the host process — no decision at all, a trivial denial-of-service against the host by any verifier that exits early; (2) a host that aborts on the write error denies before ever reading a schema-valid verdict; (3) a host that swallows the error reads stdout and relays whatever is there, including an `allow` from a verifier that demonstrably never read the request. The spec's own bound guarantees case (1)/(2)/(3) is reachable with a legitimate oversize request, and the lazy-verifier variant (emit allow, never read stdin) is the interesting hostile case: EPIPE is the one signal the host has that the request was not consumed, and the spec neither requires nor forbids acting on it. No vector exercises a verifier that exits before draining stdin; every current fixture has the verifier read stdin first.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2: "The host **MUST** write exactly one JSON object, UTF-8 encoded, to the verifier's stdin and then **MUST** close (EOF) stdin."

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §6: "A request over the bound **MUST** yield `deny code=malformed_input`; the verifier **MUST NOT** buffer an unbounded request." — a conforming verifier therefore stops reading and exits mid-write

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2 enumerates: non-zero exit; timeout; death by signal / crash; unparseable, empty, oversized, or multi-object stdout; unknown verdict / missing deny fields; schema failure — a failed request write is absent
spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §architecture pseudocode: "write(child.stdin, json(request)); close(child.stdin)" with no failure branch, unlike every downstream step which has an explicit reject()

Conformance vector index (set 0.6.0): `host-deny-no-output-timeout` — "the verifier reads stdin, writes nothing…"; `host-deny-partial-json-timeout`, `host-deny-oversize-stdout` — all fixtures consume stdin before misbehaving; none exits before stdin is drained

Runnable: `npx @bolyra/evc-conformance --host "<cmd>"` with a proposed fixture verifier `exec 0<&-; printf '{"verdict":"deny","code":"malformed_input","message":"unread"}'; exit 0` driven with a request whose bundle exceeds the OS pipe buffer (≥ 256 KiB) so the host's write cannot complete before the close

candidate.title: All 28 conformance vectors test the host's handling of verifier stdout; none tests the host's own §2 request obligations (single object, stdin EOF, required fields, positive integer now_unix), which AuthZEN-style PEP/PDP interop tests on both sides
candidate.claim: The AuthZEN family (COAZ/AARP, already a threat card) publishes interop testing where the PEP's request is validated against the request schema, not just the PDP's response. EVC's host-conformance suite is asymmetric: every vector in set 0.6.0 is a verdict-side stimulus (malformed stdout, timeout, signal, nonce reserve). A host that never closes stdin, writes two request objects, omits `granted_capabilities`, or sends `now_unix` as a float or string can still pass 28/28, because the fixture verifiers never assert anything about the bytes they received. Since SPEC HARDNESS is scored on the fraction of normative MUSTs covered by a vector, the §2 host MUSTs are an uncovered block. The gap is closable without a wire change: a request-validating fixture verifier reads stdin to EOF, parses exactly one object, checks the §2.2 schema, and returns `allow` only if the host's request was conformant, otherwise `deny code=malformed_input`. The expected host outcome flips: a non-conforming host observes a deny and the runner records a FAIL on a vector whose expected decision is allow.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2: 'The host MUST write exactly one JSON object, UTF-8 encoded, to the verifier's stdin and then MUST close (EOF) stdin. The host MUST NOT write more than one object, trailing bytes, or a stream of objects.'
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.1: '`now_unix` (integer, REQUIRED, positive)' and '`granted_capabilities` (array of strings, REQUIRED) ... An empty array is permitted.'

Conformance vector index, set 0.6.0: 28 vectors, all named host-allow-* / host-deny-* / host-nonce-*, each described as a verifier stdout/exit/nonce stimulus; no vector description mentions the request the host wrote.

Runnable: `npx @bolyra/evc-conformance --host "<cmd>"` (vector set 0.6.0) — the HUT environment convention in §16 already lets a fixture verifier be any executable, so a request-validating fixture needs no runner change.
Threat board card ecosystem-scout-authzen-coaz-aarp-mcp-decision-envelope: AuthZEN defines a request/decision envelope where both sides are schema-bound.
